title: VR for Skill Learning
subtitle: Exploring how virtual reality can support practical skill learning through physical interaction, procedural guidance, and spatial exploration.

assignments.title: Wheel Removal Training
assignments.description: A VR procedural training experience that teaches the sequence of removing a vehicle wheel through direct interaction with tools, guided actions, and immediate feedback.
assignments.note: Wall-mounted instructions and object highlights guide each action. Step gates keep the procedure in order; corrective messages explain what to do next while preserving valid progress.
assignments.detail: Snap targets reduce placement precision, while the wrench still requires socket alignment. The next suggested lug nut glows green in a star pattern; the remaining nuts glow blue. After 18 seconds without progress, required highlights become brighter and pulse faster.

steps.title: Position the jack
steps.description: Align the jack with its highlighted target beneath the car, keeping the base grounded.

steps.title: Loosen the five lug nuts
steps.description: Slightly loosen every nut while the wheel is on the ground. The green highlight suggests the next nut in a star pattern.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.description: Pump the jack handle to lift the vehicle. This step unlocks after all five nuts have been loosened.

steps.title: Remove and store the wheel
steps.description: Fully remove the nuts, pull off the wheel, and secure it in the designated rack to complete training.

assignments.topic: Spatial Navigation, Teleportation and Scene Switching
assignments.title: Garage Ready
assignments.description: A VR learning experience where users navigate between a home garage and an auto parts store, locate supplies, organize equipment, and reuse tools across multiple preparation tasks.
assignments.note: Three tasks cover tire care, wiper care, and oil service preparation. Inventory and storage locations persist between scenes during the session, so earlier purchases can become tools for later tasks.
assignments.detail: Teleportation, continuous movement, and 45-degree snap turning are available together. Overhead signs, a store directory, north-up maps, and a left-hand checklist support wayfinding. Labeled exit doors switch scenes with a fade and a short arrival sound. Headset comfort still needs evaluation.

spaces.title: Home Garage
spaces.description: Store purchases, retrieve reusable tools, and prepare the workbench. New purchases count as ready after storage; reused tools must reach the bench.

spaces.title: Auto Parts Store
spaces.description: Navigate six departments, use the directory and overhead signs, and collect the missing supplies on the checklist. Return through a labeled exit door.

closing: A sequence to follow. A space to remember. Tools to put into practice.
reflection: These projects explore different parts of skill learning: procedural guidance, spatial familiarity, and hands-on preparation. The collection will grow as new assignments explore other skills and interaction systems. Learning benefits remain design goals, rather than measured outcomes.
